gap: B draws neither of the two hairlines that give A its structure. There is no 1 px #CBCCCC rule where the Organizer (#EAEBEB) meets the File List (#FCFCFC), only a bare change of ground, and no #E1E1E1 rule under the List header and Sort pill. The header, pill and first row sit on one undivided white field, and the Organizer–List seam reads soft next to A's.
gapTheirs: The list starts about 42 px lower (first document name baseline at about y=286 against y=244). Its header takes about 170 px against B's 130 px, so on the same pane height roughly one fewer 136 px row of manuscripts is visible before the Filter field. Some of that height is the window's own toolbar buttons.
verdict: The two lists are nearly the same: 136 px row pitch in both, name at grey 25, date and two-line excerpt in the same grey 153, the same 3 px accent bar with no fill, and the same #EDEDED row rules. The difference is in the structure. A draws a rule under its header and a hairline between its columns, so the list reads as a separate, bounded object. B leaves both out, so its title, pill and rows float on one white field, and its pane edge is only a change of ground. A writer would trust either list with a manuscript, but A looks finished and B looks like an early build of it.

states.name: search
states.gap: B's Filter field holding `sea` has no clear (✕) button and no focus ring. A draws a ~4 px blue focus halo and a round dark-grey ✕ at the field's right end; B's field has a 1 px grey (#dadada-ish) outline and nothing else, so B never shows that a search is live and there's no one-click way out of it.
states.gapTheirs: The List's header is 57 px taller: A's Sort pill ends at y≈152 and the hairline under it sits at y=170, while B's pill ends at y=113. A's first result name sits at y≈222 against B's y≈180, which is ~42 px of chrome before the first manuscript at the same 136 px row pitch.
states.verdict: Both panes use the same grounds (Organizer #EAEBEB, List #FCFCFC), the same 153-grey dates and excerpts, the same 136 px rows and the same accent bar. That leaves the frame around the search to decide it. B's search looks like an idle text box: no ring, no ✕, no hairline between the Sort pill and the first row, and no rule under the last row. With the filter left on, a writer could easily think half their manuscripts had gone missing. A says loudly that you're in a search and how to get out, and that's the one I'd trust with a book.
